query_family: recovery-proof completeness + expected-subject inventory + multi-engine semantic restore + fail-open validation
notes: Best result: FireDrill shows a general completeness law: an evidence set cannot prove the absence of a missing subject without an independently supplied expected-subject inventory. Its tests make missing, stale, failed and unsigned evidence fail when subjects are scoped, while control-level grouping can mask a failing sibling workload and must not be used alone for assurance. Dune supplies a rare PostgreSQL+RabbitMQ semantic recovery analogue. query_family: physical-action restart + identity continuity + local CANCELLED/UNKNOWN + retry gate
queries: MADSci advanced error recovery retry circuit breaker
best_result: MADSci restart is a stronger ambiguity boundary than previously recorded: Engine startup cancels active workflows without first reconciling the external action, cancel_workflow overwrites the current step result with a fresh ActionResult ULID, and later retry can create a fresh ActionRequest ULID. Prior identity may remain in history but is not consulted before local finality. Exactly-once physical action across restart is therefore unproven; EXP-007 needs a process-kill fixture with durable vendor/device operation identity and explicit CONFIRMED_APPLIED / RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED / SAFE_TO_REISSUE dispositions.
